title: Messi to Get Buenos Aires Farewell in Final Argentina Appearance on Oct. 6
excerpt: Named to Lionel Scaloni's squad despite retiring from international football on Aug. 31, Messi will play only the Oct. 6 friendly against Benin at the Estadio Monumental — his 208th cap and official send-off before Argentina's home fans.
body:
• Lionel Messi was named in Lionel Scaloni's squad for Argentina's three October friendlies despite announcing his international retirement on August 31.
  • He will play only the October 6 match against Benin at Buenos Aires' 85,000-capacity Estadio Monumental — expected to be his 208th and final Argentina cap.
  • Argentina's football association has invited the 2022 World Cup-winning squad and their families for what it calls Messi's official send-off.
  • Messi's club career with Inter Miami continues; the farewell comes after Argentina's 1-0 loss to Spain in the World Cup final.

The international window that was supposed to open a new era for Argentina without Lionel Messi will instead close one. Head coach Lionel Scaloni included Messi in his squad for next month's friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin — all to be played in Buenos Aires — and the final of the three will double as Messi's official farewell in front of his home fans.

The 39-year-old will feature only in the October 6 match against Benin at River Plate's Estadio Monumental, according to reports and Argentina's football association. Since he announced his international retirement, the sense in Argentina was that walking away without one last appearance on home soil would have been a strangely quiet ending for the country's greatest player.

A farewell three months in the making

Messi said on August 31 that he had "nothing left to give" to the national team, ending a two-decade international career that finally peaked with the 2022 World Cup title in Qatar and Copa America triumphs in 2021 and 2024. His bid for back-to-back World Cups ended in heartbreak this year: eight goals and four assists across the tournament, then a 1-0 defeat to Spain in the final.

"Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I've given it my all, I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some really great young players coming through behind me who deserve their chance."

— Lionel Messi

The Benin friendly changes the terms of the goodbye. The Argentinian Football Association said in a statement that it had invited Messi so "he can receive the send-off he truly deserves on October 6 here in Argentina." The association added that it had also invited all of the world champions who played alongside him at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to join him, together with their families.

Giovani Lo Celso and Messi's Inter Miami teammate Rodrigo De Paul were likewise named only for the Benin match, a detail that has prompted speculation about their own international futures.

Context: the end of the Scaloni-Messi era

The October window — Bolivia on September 30, Burkina Faso on October 3, Benin on October 6 — was meant to be Scaloni's first squad of the post-Messi era, a chance to blood the generation Messi himself said deserved its chance. Instead it becomes a transition staged around one night. Messi retires as Argentina's all-time record appearance maker and scorer, with 208 caps and 125 goals.

His club career, at least, is not done: Messi remains an active Inter Miami player in MLS, which means this farewell is strictly an Argentina affair — the albiceleste jersey retired while the club shirt carries on.

What it means for India

Few places outside Argentina will feel the weight of that jersey's retirement more than India. Messi's fanbase in the country has long been its own phenomenon — giant cutouts of the Argentine still dot towns across Kerala, and Kolkata's relationship with him stretches back 15 years to his first visit to Salt Lake Stadium, where he captained Argentina for the first time in a friendly against Venezuela in 2011.

The attachment runs deep enough that fans have reshaped their lives around it. Soumindra Ghosh, owner of Kolkata's Messi-themed Dum Dum Leo Cafe, told PTI that Messi's retirement felt like "being with Messi in sorrow, being with Messi in joy" — and that he plans to mark the occasion by recording videos with visitors and serving his "La Pulga" dish for free. A friend got a Messi tattoo on his hand on retirement day, saying, "Messi finished his journey on the pitch, but now Messi will stay with me forever."

Former India player KT Chacko described the retirement as a "huge shock" for the game's fans in Kerala, where he said he would stay awake late into the night to watch Messi play. "I am not an Argentina fan, but I am a Messi fan," Chacko told ANI. "The thought that we may not be able to see him in that jersey anymore is truly heartbreaking."

Kolkata's Messi story carries a scar too: his December 2024 "GOAT Tour" stop at Salt Lake Stadium ended in chaos when fans who had paid up to Rs 14,000 barely glimpsed him before he left early over safety concerns, prompting an apology from chief minister Mamata Banerjee and a probe into the mismanagement. For many in the city, that tarnished evening makes October 6 — even watched from 9,000 miles away — the proper goodbye they never got.

What's next

The October 6 match is now the calendar's emotional centerpiece: 85,000 fans at the Monumental, the 2022 champions reunited, and one last night in the albiceleste for the captain who carried it for 20 years. After that, Scaloni's real rebuild begins — and Messi's India fans will hold on to one last hope: a prospective Inter Miami pre-season tour in South Asia, and perhaps one more glimpse of the man Kolkata says it is "not yet ready to say goodbye" to.
image_caption: Lionel Messi, who will play his final Argentina match at Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental on October 6 against Benin.
nri_angle: Messi's retirement lands hardest in Kerala and Kolkata, home to some of the world's most devoted Messi fanbases — from Kerala's ubiquitous giant cutouts to Kolkata's Messi-themed cafe — and for many Indian fans the Oct. 6 farewell is the proper goodbye they never got after the chaotic 2024 GOAT Tour stop.
